questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I carefully reviewed the curriculum to ensure that the subjects aligned with my degree program and would allow me to gain relevant knowledge while also exploring new academic perspectives. Additionally, I considered the cultural and social environment of the host country. I was eager to experience a different culture, lifestyle, and educational system. The opportunity to travel and explore nearby countries was another motivating factor.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should know that living off campus can be a very rewarding experience, but it also requires independence and good organization. One of the biggest advantages is having more freedom and privacy compared to student dormitories. Living in the city, especially in the center of Prague, allowed me to feel more integrated into local life rather than staying in a student-only environment.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Overall, I was quite successful in registering for the classes I wanted. At first, I was placed on a waiting list for some of my preferred courses, which made the process slightly stressful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My main advice to future exchange students regarding registration is not to get too attached to the courses you initially planned to take from home. Even if you carefully select your preferred subjects in advance, availability can change, classes may be full, or schedules might overlap once you arrive.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching at my host institution was somewhat different from that at University of Copenhagen (UCPH). One of the main differences was the stronger emphasis on active participation. In many classes, students were expected to contribute regularly to discussions, share their opinions, and engage directly with the material during lectures.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: At Charles University, there was a wide range of cultural, athletic, and social activities available for students, especially for exchange students. The university, together with student organizations such as the Erasmus Student Network (ESN), organized welcome events, city tours, social gatherings, language exchanges, and themed international evenings. These activities made it easy to meet other students and feel integrated into the international community.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: One important piece of advice for future exchange students at Charles University is to be proactive from the very beginning. Whether it concerns course registration, accommodation, or social activities, taking initiative and staying organized makes the transition much easier.
